answer: An agent economy can price sybil identity by making standing accrue, not bought. Each agent must forge a public record of graded work: claims are scored by randomly assigned peers, and part of the balance is locked against each unresolved claim. A fresh key is cheap to mint but inherits nothing, so a velvet crowd of ten thousand names hides no history — each pays full verification cost alone, and its stake is forfeit when peers find nothing behind it. Reputation, the pearl worth stealing, cannot be transferred in bulk, so attacking at scale costs O(n) graded work per identity instead of O(1).
